changelog:
[pre-print cut 2026-08-03, rel#29] Reduce avg holdings 5.6→4.9 via per-sleeve equity min_position_pct=8 (bonds stay diversified). Loss metrics improve: worst-12mo −4.3→−3.7, worst calendar year +1.4→+2.4 (0 down years/21), Martin 5.21→5.26; intra-period give w3m −0.7pp, maxDD −0.9pp. D6 relative-to-60/40 regresses (foregone gains in bulls) — accepted per Preserve's loss-averse mandate.

[D6 regression accepted on RDD3y, worst-3y excess, longest underwater (d): Preserve customers are loss-sensitive, not gain-sensitive. The regressed D6 metrics (worst-3y-EXCESS, longest-RELATIVE-underwater) are all relative to 60/40 and the damage is foregone gains during UPTRENDS, not absolute loss. On the metrics this segment feels, concentration IMPROVES: worst-12mo −4.3→−3.7, worst calendar year +1.4→+2.4 (still 0 down years in 21), and it fell LESS than 60/40 in every crisis window. Preserve is gated on ABSOLUTE loss, not relative-to-60/40.]

[pre-print cut 2026-08-10, rel#30] Retire the ratchet re-risk override and arm cash momentum for an empty defensive sleeve. The override let a gated-out bond sleeve re-risk its vacated weight into equity, so Preserve held ZERO ballast in 12 of the 14 months where every bond failed the gate, contradicting its own floor: 0.4. The allocator also read defensive momentum as a fabricated 0 in those months ('there are no bonds', not 'bonds returned zero'); it now uses the TBILL_13W trailing return over the same 18-month window, compared against undiscounted risk momentum. CAGR 16.68% -> 15.73%, maxDD -16.49% -> -13.78%, worst-12mo -3.69% -> -3.44%, Copley 4.516 -> 4.572. The floor was swept 0.20-0.60 to test whether the CAGR was recoverable; it is not without selling the risk profile, and 0.40 already sits on the Martin plateau (4.88-4.96 across 0.40-0.48). D6: RDD3y improves 35%, longest-underwater 1035d -> 1150d accepted, see the acceptance reason.

[D6 regression accepted on longest underwater (d): RDD3y IMPROVES 35% (0.5301% -> 0.3451%) — the relative-downside measure the D6/SPY-lag work itself settled on as the right instrument. worst-3y excess and cohorts-still-behind are UNCHANGED. Longest underwater grows 1035d -> 1150d, which is the direct and predictable cost of holding 40% ballast through a recovery instead of re-risking to 100% equity. That re-risking is exactly the behaviour being retired: the old book held ZERO ballast in 12 of the 14 months where every bond failed the gate, contradicting its own floor: 0.4. Taken because a Preserve model that abandons its ballast promise in the months ballast matters is not the product, at any CAGR. The floor was swept 0.20-0.60 to test whether the cost was avoidable; it is not without selling the risk profile.]

[pre-print cut 2026-08-10, rel#31] Engine-only re-cut; the config gains dust_prune_pct: 0.1 as a guard (Preserve had no sub-0.1% dust to begin with) and is otherwise unchanged. (1) dynamic_k and the per-sleeve minimum-position floor were rescaling survivors blindly after dropping a holding, breaching the per-fund cap that crowd_deconcentrate had tightened precisely to spread a crowded book — SOXX reached 43.17% against a 37.10% cap on 2018-10-01. Both stages now share a water-fill that pins holdings at the cap and leaves residue the caps cannot absorb unallocated. (2) An empty target map means 100% CASH, not a failed rebalance: the executor was holding the previous month's book while the engine asked for cash. CAGR 15.7299% -> 15.6919%, Martin 4.9046 -> 4.8759; maxDD and worst-12mo bit-identical. The 2022 bear now reads -0.60% rather than +2.45%: the engine wanted 100% cash on 2022-10-03 when every fund in the universe failed the gate, and the old executor rode the November bounce instead. That credential was flattered by the model being overruled. Numbered v6.4 alongside Growth; v6.3 was cut, rolled back, and is permanently bound in the public version registry to a different fingerprint.

[pre-print cut 2026-08-16, rel#32] Engine all-cash liquidation fix; config unchanged from v6.4 (the cash-momentum lever stands on Preserve on its honest trade: -0.79pp CAGR for +2.9pp maxDD, re-measured on the fixed engine). One all-cash month now trades instead of silently holding the prior book.

— superseded in place 2026-08-20 —
Defensive ratchet 1.0 -> 0.75. Full ratchet was a dominated endpoint: 0.75 delivers +0.34pp CAGR (15.36% -> 15.70%) at IDENTICAL max drawdown (-13.78%), a materially better worst-12mo (-4.41% -> -3.44%) and Copley 3.49 -> 4.56. Max drawdown FLOORS from 0.75 upward, so past that point extra cash buys no drawdown protection and only costs return, while worst-12mo falls off a cliff exactly at the 1.0 endpoint. Found by sweeping the interior (0/.125/.25/.375/.5/.625/.75/.875/1) - an endpoints-only comparison reads this as a CAGR-vs-drawdown tradeoff that does not actually exist. Acceptance passed with D6 IMPROVING (RDD3y 7.7435% -> 6.4071%, cohorts-behind 18.30% -> 14.50%, other two unchanged), stress gate pass, Martin up in both halves. 13 of 248 rebalances changed. Growth is unaffected and stays at ratchet 0, where it is monotonically optimal.
